sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the learned Trial Court has committed error in dismissing the complaint though NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/360/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined the offence was made out.
The respondent No.2 being an employee of the complainant, collected bill amount of Rs.7,78,140/- from the customers of the complainant company and kept in his possession.
In this regard, to repay, the respondent No.2 accepted his mistake and executed notarized document and thereafter, he failed to pay the said amount.
In view of the above, he has committed offence of cheating and criminal breach of trust.
Though sufficient evidence led, learned Trial Court has committed error in dismissing the complaint.

Hence, he has requested to quash and set aside the order passed by learned Additional CJM, Ahmedabad Rural,
register the complaint and issue process against the accused persons.
4) Learned counsel for respondent Nos.2 and 3 has raised objection qua straightaway approached this Court.

The applicant has not preferred revision application before the learned Sessions Court and he has relied on the decisions of Rajasthan High Court (Jaipur Bench) in S.B.Criminal Misc.
(Petition) No.8225/2024 and Jharkhand High court (Ranchi Bench) in Criminal Revision No.417/2023.
Further he has argued that the dispute is civil in nature and no documentary evidence led by the complainant qua alleged amount.
Promissory note is executed.
No other litigation has been filed.
Hence, he has requested to dismiss the revision application.

5) So far as the maintainability of the revision application is concerned, both the High Court as well as the learned Sessions Court have concurrent revisional jurisdiction under Sections 397 and 401 of the Cr.P.C., and even suo motu revision is permissible.
However, this Court is not inclined to deal with any further technical issues in this regard.

6) Now, coming to the merits of the case, it appears that a complaint under Section 202 of the Cr.P.C. was filed before the learned JMFC, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/360/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined Ahmedabad Rural, against accused Nos. 1 and 2.
Accused No. 2 is the wife of accused No. 1 and has no connection whatsoever with the alleged offence.

The only allegation against accused No. 1 is that the complainant was engaged in business, and accused No. 1,
being his employee, collected money on behalf of the complainant's company but failed to return the same.
It is alleged that accused No. 1 collected an amount of Rs. 7,78,140/- from customers but did not remit it to the complainant.
In this regard, it is stated that accused No. 1 executed a mortgage deed on a Rs. 100 stamp paper and also issued a promissory note.
Thereafter, part payment was made by him.

The complaint under Section 202 of the Cr.P.C. was subjected to inquiry, and the Police Inspector submitted a report clearly opining that there were no allegations against accused No. 2 and that she had no involvement in the alleged offence.
After considering the said document produced before learned Magistrate, ld. Magistrate came to the conclusion that no case is made out as civil is dispute in nature.

Considering the fact that promissory note is issued towards security and mortgaged deed is also executed and settlement took place, question does not arise to issue process against the accused under Sections 406 and 420 of IPC, more particularly after settlement part payment had been made.
7) In view of the above, it is evident that there was no intention to cheat from the outset.

Therefore,
the alleged offence under Sections 406 and 420 of the IPC cannot be said to be made out.
The dispute is essentially civil in nature, and it appears that an attempt has been made to cloak a civil recovery matter as a criminal proceeding.

9) Even after the pronouncement of Priti Saraf & Anr. (supra), the Hon'ble Apex Court has delivered a judgment in case of Rikhab Birani & Anr. vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr. reported in 2025 INSC 512 and Rekha Jain vs. The State of Karnataka & Anr. reported in 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 468 and clarified the position of law when offence under Section 406 or 420 of IPC is made out.

Hence, no interference is required by this Court.
Hence, present revision application fails and is hereby dismissed.
